After taking the aforementioned actions, the Parties will establish a mechanism to continue discussions about economic and trade relations. The representative from the Chinese side for these discussions will be He Lifeng, Vice Premier of the State Council, and the representatives from the U.S. side will be Scott Bessent, Secretary of the Treasury, and Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative. These discussions may be conducted alternately in China and the United States, or a third country upon agreement of the Parties. As required, the two sides may conduct working-level consultations on relevant economic and trade issues. https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/05/joint-statement-on-u-s-china-economic-and-trade-meeting-in-geneva/ Updated on April 25th **Presidential Executive Order on Tariff Adjustments for Chinese Goods** On April 8, 2025 (local time), U.S. President Donald Trump issued an executive order announcing the following tariff measures on goods originating from China (including Hong Kong, China): 1. **Elimination of De Minimis Exemption for Chinese-origin Goods** 2. **Additional 125%+20% (If it is the category under 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, the tariff exemption is 125%) Tariff on High-value Chinese Goods** 3.Fedex Official: For B2C shipments, a valid FedEx account number is required. 4.If the product falls under HTS categories 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 125% tariff exemption. However, DHL’s customs declaration system may inaccurately apply or fail to recognize the 125% exemption. If the recipient finds that the product is indeed eligible for the exemption but the 125% duty relief was not applied, they must file a dispute with DHL immediately, as there is a strict deadline for appeals. By the time the sender notices the issue, the appeal window may have already closed. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. It’s Trickier Than You Think. But because of an ever-changing patchwork of trade rules, not every product will be charged an astronomical tariff, trade lawyers, customs brokers and importers say. In some cases, tariffs will pile on other tariffs. In other instances, they can reduce costs, while other times they can cancel out new ones. The new 125 percent rate that President Trump imposed will in many cases be added on top of long-existing duties. There are four main categories of tariffs that are imposed on goods from China. Note: The tariff on auto parts comes into effect in early May. The average provided for the base rate is calculated by the World Trade Organization, which computes an average of all tariff lines. Since the first exhibition was held in 1964, electronica has gradually grown and now covers the entire world of electronics, including the micro- and nano-worlds of semiconductor and micro systems technology, as well as measurement and sensor technology, display technology and vehicle electronics, etc., which is the best choice for any technology enthusiasts and industry practitioners. PCBWay has participated in theelectronica many times and has received a warm response every time. At the exhibition, everyone has the opportunity to get close to our various products and fully evaluate the performance and quality of our products, which is far beyond the scope of online communication. On-site interaction gives us the opportunity to answer everyone's questions in a timely manner and help them understand the products more comprehensively, thereby accelerating the process of cooperation. Therefore, after the exhibition, we not only strengthened our cooperation with existing customers, but also successfully attracted the attention of many new potential partners. PCBWay will certainly not be absent from this year's exhibition.In addition, in order to give everyone a better exhibition experience and also to show how much importance PCBWay attaches to this exhibition, this year we made some innovations: Time: 2024.11.12-2024.11.15 Location: Trade Fair Center Messe München, Germany PCBWay Booth No.: A1.163 Highlights: Color- printed Boards In addition to the PCB series products, 3D printed parts and sheet metal parts that we have been displaying in the past, we will also bring the latest color-printed board samples. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad by: PCBWay Oct 11,2023 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Recently, PCBWay added a plug-in called PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit to Kicad: With just one click of the mouse, four files can be exported from the layout file automatically: Gerber file, IPC-Netlist file, BOM file and Pick and Place file, which can significantly improves the efficiency of pre-production work. Installation from the Official KiCad Repositories After installation, the plugin will appear on the right side of the navigation bar. And users can use it to export all the production files with just a click. Process demonstration： Sending the files to PCBWay, and they can be used for production after being reviewed by the staff. Note: If you want to place an assembly order, please be sure to add MPN information to the BOM. This can help the quoter source the devices you need more accurately. Manual installation Except for the way mentioned before, you can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Fabrication-Toolkit-for-KiCad: Open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About BOM Through BOM files, we can get all information of the components used in your design. In order to speed up the quotation process, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) If you have more suggestions, please leave a message below, PCBWay has committed to providing everyone with high-quality services. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > Turning Student Ideas into Real Projects with the PCBWay Future Innovators Program Turning Student Ideas into Real Projects with the PCBWay Future Innovators Program by: Mila Sep 15,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News For students, turning an engineering idea into a working prototype is an important part of learning. But moving from a schematic or CAD model to a manufactured product can be challenging when budget and access to manufacturing resources are limited. The PCBWay Future Innovators Program is designed to help students and educational institutions bridge that gap. By providing manufacturing support for eligible educational and non-commercial projects, PCBWay helps students gain hands-on experience and turn their ideas into real, testable hardware. Why Hands-On Manufacturing Matters for Students Engineering education goes beyond textbooks and simulations. Designing a circuit, creating a PCB, building a mechanical enclosure, and testing a working prototype allow students to understand how engineering concepts translate into real-world products. For many student projects, however, manufacturing can become a practical challenge. Prototype costs, limited access to equipment, and the difficulty of producing small quantities may prevent students from taking a project beyond the design stage. This is where manufacturing support can make a difference. With the Future Innovators Program, eligible students can receive support for projects related to education, research, competitions, graduation projects, open-source development, and social-impact innovation. Supporting Student Projects from PCB to Prototype The program is intended to support more than just PCB fabrication. Eligible manufacturing charges can include: PCB manufacturing PCBA assembly services 3D printing CNC machining Sheet metal fabrication Other approved in-house manufacturing services This gives students more flexibility when developing complete prototypes that combine electronics, mechanical parts, and enclosures. For example, a robotics team may need a custom PCB, CNC-machined structural parts, and 3D-printed components. A student developing an IoT device may need both PCB assembly and a custom enclosure. By bringing these manufacturing capabilities together, PCBWay can help students move more efficiently from concept to physical prototype. Support for Individual Students and Schools The Future Innovators Program provides two support options based on who is purchasing and how the products will be used. Individual Student Projects Verified students working on educational, research, competition, graduation, or non-commercial maker projects can receive 50% off eligible manufacturing charges, up to USD 200 per approved project. The support is project-specific and intended for genuine student participation. Commercial production, resale, and customer-delivery orders are not eligible. School Educational Purchases Schools, departments, laboratories, and educational programs can apply for expanded support when purchasing products for classroom teaching, laboratory training, workshops, or student projects. Eligible school purchases can receive 50% off eligible manufacturing charges, up to USD 2,000 per approved purchase. This option can be particularly useful for educators who need multiple PCBs or prototype parts for laboratory exercises, teaching kits, workshops, or student training. What Types of Projects Can Apply? The program is designed around practical learning and innovation. Eligible projects can include: Course & Lab Projects — curriculum-based assignments, experiments, and engineering exercises Research Prototypes — academic research, thesis projects, and proof-of-concept development Student Competitions — robotics, electronics, automation, and engineering competitions Graduation Projects — capstone and final-year engineering projects Open-Source & Maker Projects — student-led, non-commercial projects that encourage learning and sharing Social-Impact Innovation — projects focused on environmental, accessibility, education, or community needs Classroom & Lab Batches — manufacturing support for institutional teaching and training The goal is not simply to reduce manufacturing costs, but to make it easier for students to learn by building. From Design Files to a Working Prototype A student project often develops through several stages: defining a problem, designing the solution, creating hardware, manufacturing prototypes, testing the result, and improving the design. Manufacturing is an important part of this process. A fabricated PCB can reveal layout or assembly issues that are difficult to identify from a schematic alone. A 3D-printed enclosure can expose mechanical interference. A CNC-machined part can help students evaluate fit, strength, and usability. These iterations turn manufacturing into part of the learning experience rather than simply the final step of a project. How the Future Innovators Program Works Applying for the program is designed to be straightforward: 01 — Create a Quote Prepare the relevant PCBWay quotation or order for your project. 02 — Submit Your Application Provide your student or institutional information, project details, and quote or order number. 03 — Eligibility Review PCBWay reviews student status or institutional eligibility, project purpose, feasibility, branding requirements, and other program conditions. 04 — Receive the Result Approved support is linked to the verified account and designated project. 05 — Pay & Produce After approval, pay the adjusted amount and continue with the normal manufacturing process. Approved support should normally be used within 30 days, and changes to the materials or order may require another review. Helping the Next Generation Build, Test, and Learn Innovation often starts with a simple idea: a circuit a student wants to build, a robot they want to improve, or a problem they believe they can solve. At PCBWay, we believe students should have the opportunity to take those ideas beyond the screen and into the real world. Through the PCBWay Future Innovators Program, we aim to lower some of the manufacturing barriers faced by students and educational institutions while encouraging hands-on engineering, experimentation, and innovation. Whether it is a graduation project, research prototype, competition entry, classroom project, or social-impact idea, the next great project can start with a student willing to build it. Have a student project ready to build? Explore the PCBWay Future Innovators Program and see if your project qualifies for support. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. From Design Files to a Working Prototype A student project often develops through several stages: defining a problem, designing the solution, creating hardware, manufacturing prototypes, testing the result, and improving the design. Manufacturing is an important part of this process. A fabricated PCB can reveal layout or assembly issues that are difficult to identify from a schematic alone. A 3D-printed enclosure can expose mechanical interference. A CNC-machined part can help students evaluate fit, strength, and usability. These iterations turn manufacturing into part of the learning experience rather than simply the final step of a project. How the Future Innovators Program Works Applying for the program is designed to be straightforward: 01 — Create a Quote Prepare the relevant PCBWay quotation or order for your project. 02 — Submit Your Application Provide your student or institutional information, project details, and quote or order number. 03 — Eligibility Review PCBWay reviews student status or institutional eligibility, project purpose, feasibility, branding requirements, and other program conditions. 04 — Receive the Result Approved support is linked to the verified account and designated project. 05 — Pay & Produce After approval, pay the adjusted amount and continue with the normal manufacturing process. Approved support should normally be used within 30 days, and changes to the materials or order may require another review. Helping the Next Generation Build, Test, and Learn Innovation often starts with a simple idea: a circuit a student wants to build, a robot they want to improve, or a problem they believe they can solve. At PCBWay, we believe students should have the opportunity to take those ideas beyond the screen and into the real world. Through the PCBWay Future Innovators Program, we aim to lower some of the manufacturing barriers faced by students and educational institutions while encouraging hands-on engineering, experimentation, and innovation. Whether it is a graduation project, research prototype, competition entry, classroom project, or social-impact idea, the next great project can start with a student willing to build it. Unlock Color PCB Printing with PCBWay! by: PCBWay Mar 08,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Color PCB Printing PCBWay Service Nowadays, traditional PCB printing technology can no longer meet the aesthetic requirements of modern circuit board production. To better fulfill customers' design needs, we are pleased to announce that PCBWay has introduced UV printing equipment. This equipment utilizes UV-curable inks to achieve high-quality image printing on various materials, including fiberglass boards, metal substrates, ceramic substrates, flexible boards, and rigid-flex boards. Entrance https://www.pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx Prerequisites for Ordering Maximum size for a single piece: 270*470MM; Selection of background soldermask color required. Design Specifications Drill holes, traces, soldermasks, and outline designs must comply with specifications. Avoid placing colored characters in areas with solder mask openings, such as surface-mount pads or through-hole pads. What kind of files should be provided for color printing? Method One : Draw colored characters on the silkscreen layer of the Gerber and provide reference pictures. For example: Method Two : If you include information about colored silkscreen in the Gerber layer, each individual color must have its own layer. If there is only one layer, we can only print one color. [This method is not recommended] . If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. However, compared to the solder mask, it is less scratch-resistant because UV printing is ink that is sprayed on and is relatively thin. Welcome to give it a try if you're interested! Besides, PCBWay will continue to enhance its manufacturing capabilities to bring more choices and personalized services to customers in the future. The controller adopts AtomS3R, which is powered by the ESP32-S3 chip and provides a generous 8MB Flash + 8MB PSRAM memory combo. It also integrates a 9-axis IMU (BMI270 + BMM150), an IR transmitter, and other rich peripherals. The voice base is the Atomic Voice Base, built on the ES8311 audio codec, delivering high-fidelity audio decoding together with microphone and speaker driving capability. The kit supports multiple voice assistants such as XiaoZhi Voice Assistant, OpenAI Voice Assistant, and Volcano Engine Voice Assistant, enabling real-time voice interaction, custom wake-words, and low-latency recognition. Verify Now Blog > 0402 vs 0603 Capacitor for High-Speed PCB Decoupling 0402 vs 0603 Capacitor for High-Speed PCB Decoupling by: Mila Sep 16,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout decoupling capacitor 0402 capacitor 0603 capacitor 0402 vs 0603 capacitor A common misconception is that a larger capacitor package stores more energy and therefore provides better filtering performance. However, in high-speed PCB designs such as FPGA, SoC, and DDR applications, 0402 capacitors with a typical value of 0.1 μF are commonly placed near BGA core power pins instead of larger 0603 capacitors. For the same nominal capacitance, the key difference in 0402 vs 0603 capacitor performance is not how much charge the capacitor stores, but its equivalent series inductance (ESL). At lower frequencies, the performance difference between package sizes is usually less significant. As the operating frequency enters the MHz range and above, ESL increasingly affects the impedance and effective frequency range of a decoupling capacitor. The Underlying Principle: Equivalent Series Inductance (ESL) A surface-mount capacitor is not an ideal capacitor. Its equivalent circuit typically consists of an ideal capacitance (C), equivalent series resistance (ESR), and equivalent series inductance (ESL). ESL comes from the entire current path, including the internal electrodes, terminations, PCB pads, traces, and power/ground vias. Inductance opposes rapidly changing current, and its effect becomes more significant as frequency increases. Every capacitor has a self-resonant frequency (SRF): Operating frequency < SRF: The device behaves mainly as a capacitor and can perform its decoupling function normally. Operating frequency > SRF: The device gradually becomes inductive, and its high-frequency decoupling capability decreases. A higher self-resonant frequency generally means that a decoupling capacitor can maintain low impedance over a wider high-frequency range. For example, consider 0402 and 0603 capacitors with the same nominal capacitance of 0.1 μF: 0603 capacitor: Its larger body size generally results in a longer internal current path and higher intrinsic parasitic inductance. 0402 capacitor: Its smaller body size generally provides a shorter current path and lower intrinsic parasitic inductance. Therefore, under similar capacitance and component structures, a 0402 capacitor typically has lower parasitic inductance and a higher self-resonant frequency than a 0603 capacitor, making it more suitable for high-frequency decoupling. The actual ESL and SRF values should be verified from the component datasheet or the manufacturer's high-frequency model. PCB Pads and Vias Also Add Parasitic Inductance Engineers often focus only on the capacitor's intrinsic ESL specified in the datasheet. However, in a complete power delivery network, PCB pads, traces, and vias also introduce parasitic inductance and can sometimes have an even greater impact than the capacitor itself. In an 0402 vs 0603 capacitor comparison, the larger pads and spacing of a 0603 package can make the connection between the capacitor and power/ground vias longer. This additional trace length increases the total loop inductance. The smaller pads of a 0402 capacitor make it easier to place power and ground vias close to the component. When the PCB manufacturing and assembly processes allow it, microvias or Via-in-Pad can also be used to further shorten the current path and reduce the power-to-ground loop area. When an IC core suddenly draws high-frequency transient current, the total inductance of the current loop affects the power response. Even a capacitor with excellent electrical characteristics may provide limited high-frequency decoupling if the current path is too long. This is why the key advantage of a 0402 capacitor is not simply its smaller package size, but its ability to help create a smaller and lower-inductance current loop. （Optimized Layout） 0402 vs 0603 Capacitor: Advantages and Limitations Advantages of 0402 Capacitors Lower intrinsic parasitic inductance and typically higher SRF, providing better performance for high-frequency decoupling; Smaller pads allow the capacitor to be placed closer to BGA power pins and return paths, reducing the power-to-ground loop area; Higher placement density allows more decoupling capacitors to be placed around BGA devices, helping optimize PDN impedance; The smaller package makes it easier to implement compact power and ground via arrangements and, when supported by the PCB process, microvia or Via-in-Pad structures. Limitations of 0402 Capacitors In the same component series, the available capacitance and voltage-rating options may be more limited, while the actual effective capacitance can also decrease under DC bias; For the same capacitance and voltage rating, the component cost may be higher than that of a 0603 capacitor; Manual soldering is more difficult, with a higher risk of insufficient soldering or component loss, and mass production requires tighter stencil and placement process control; At relatively low frequencies, the performance difference between 0402 and 0603 is usually small, so a 0402 capacitor does not need to be selected simply because it is smaller. When to Use 0603 Capacitors They can generally provide sufficient performance in lower-frequency filtering applications; The larger package can make it easier to obtain suitable capacitance, voltage ratings, and mechanical reliability; They are easier to solder manually and can be suitable for general power filtering and decoupling applications where high-frequency performance is not the primary concern. Therefore, the choice between an 0402 vs 0603 capacitor should not be based on a fixed frequency boundary. As frequency increases, the ESL differences introduced by the component package and PCB mounting structure become increasingly important. The actual selection should consider effective capacitance, ESR, ESL, SRF, and the PCB layout together. Key Considerations for Decoupling Capacitor Selection and Layout Place decoupling capacitors as close as possible to BGA core power pins and other power pins that require high-frequency transient current. A 0402 capacitor is often preferred for these applications. The goal is to reduce the total parasitic inductance of the current loop and improve high-frequency PDN impedance. For DC-DC outputs and other applications where mounting inductance is less critical, 0603 or even 0805 packages can be selected according to effective capacitance, voltage rating, cost, and manufacturing requirements. Loop area is more important than package size alone. This is a common misconception in PCB decoupling. A 0402 capacitor placed far away from the IC power and return path may provide poorer high-frequency performance than a 0603 capacitor placed directly along the current path. Package size is only one factor affecting parasitic inductance. The total power-to-ground loop inductance is more important. Component placement, pad design, and via location all play an important role in PCB decoupling. Do not blindly move to a 0201 package. As the package becomes smaller, the reduction in ESL can provide diminishing returns because the PCB mounting structure can become a larger part of the total inductance. At the same time, soldering difficulty, placement requirements, and component costs may increase. A 0402 capacitor is therefore a common balance between performance, board space, and manufacturing cost in many high-speed PDN designs, although the final package should always be selected according to the specific device and manufacturing process. Common Misconceptions About Decoupling Capacitors ❌ Misconception 1: A larger capacitor package stores more energy and therefore provides better decoupling. ✅ Reality: Under the same effective capacitance and operating conditions, package size itself does not determine how much energy a capacitor stores. The high-frequency performance difference between an 0402 capacitor and a 0603 capacitor mainly comes from parasitic parameters associated with the capacitor and its PCB mounting structure, with ESL being an important factor. ❌ Misconception 2: If the capacitance is the same, the package does not matter. ✅ Reality: Even with the same nominal capacitance, different packages can have different ESL, ESR, and SRF characteristics. During decoupling capacitor selection and PDN impedance simulation, models that match the actual component and PCB mounting structure should be used whenever possible. Otherwise, the simulated impedance curve and resonance characteristics may differ significantly from the actual result. For high-speed PCB decoupling, component selection should therefore go beyond nominal capacitance. The package, effective capacitance, ESL, SRF, and—most importantly—the complete current-loop PCB layout should all be considered. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > High-Speed ADC PCB Layout Guide: EPAD, PDS, and Grounding Best Practices High-Speed ADC PCB Layout Guide: EPAD, PDS, and Grounding Best Practices by: Mila Sep 10,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout high speed analog to digital converter high speed adc adc layout adc pcb design High-speed analog-to-digital converter (ADC) PCB layout involves multiple design parameters, and their importance varies depending on the application. For high-speed ADC systems, the focus should not be on optimizing every routing detail, but on avoiding common design deviations and maintaining the overall performance of the signal chain. For a broader overview of PCB Layout principles, designers should also consider signal integrity, power integrity, grounding, and return paths as part of the overall design. 1. EPAD Design Guidelines for ADC PCB Design The exposed pad (EPAD), defined as Pin 0 by ADI, is the core pad located on the bottom of many integrated circuit packages. It typically provides the main grounding and thermal connection and serves as an important path for the internal ground structure. Some converters and amplifiers do not have dedicated ground pins, with their grounding function primarily relying on the EPAD. Therefore, EPAD design directly affects electrical connection stability and thermal performance and should not be overlooked in ADC PCB design. The EPAD must form a reliable solder connection with the PCB to ensure both electrical and thermal connectivity. Poor soldering or insufficient contact can lead to abnormal grounding, inadequate heat dissipation, and even malfunction of the signal chain. For reliable EPAD performance, three key aspects should be considered in ADC PCB design. Multilayer Grounding and Thermal Copper According to the device datasheet and overall thermal requirements, grounding and thermal copper structures can be added on the appropriate PCB layers. These structures should provide reliable electrical and thermal connections to the PCB ground planes, helping improve heat dissipation, particularly in high-power and multichannel signal-chain applications. The bottom layer can also incorporate a corresponding grounding or thermal area when required by the device and system design. Depending on the application, this area can support grounding, thermal management, high-frequency decoupling, or mechanical positioning for a bottom-side thermal structure. （exposed pad pcb design） EPAD Pad Segmentation A large EPAD can be divided into multiple smaller areas using a cross-hatched stencil pattern or solder mask segmentation. During reflow soldering, solder paste distribution can vary across a large continuous pad, potentially resulting in uneven soldering, voids, or insufficient effective contact. Proper EPAD segmentation helps improve solder paste distribution and create a more uniform and stable connection between the device and PCB, improving both electrical and thermal reliability. EPAD Ground Vias and Via Filling Ground vias can be added to individual EPAD sections according to the device recommendations and PCB manufacturing requirements. Whether these vias require solder paste filling, epoxy filling, or other treatment depends on the via dimensions, pad structure, and manufacturing process. For via structures that may allow solder paste to flow into the holes during reflow, appropriate via filling or solder mask treatment should be considered. This helps reduce soldering defects and improves the reliability of the EPAD electrical and thermal connection. (EPAD design: large vs segmented) 2. Power Decoupling and PDS Design for High-Speed ADC The primary goal of PCB power decoupling is to reduce the impedance of the power delivery system (PDS) to ground. A common mistake is to place large numbers of capacitors with different capacitance values without considering their actual frequency response. In practice, a large number of redundant capacitors is not always necessary. Carefully selecting capacitors based on capacitance, component type, package, and process characteristics can optimize PDS impedance while saving PCB space and reducing component cost. Redundant capacitors can introduce layout congestion, additional cost, and potential resonance risks. They do not inherently violate PCB manufacturing requirements, but excessive or poorly planned decoupling can reduce overall design efficiency. Capacitor Selection and PCB Decoupling Layout The performance of a capacitor varies with its package and construction. Even capacitors from the same supplier can have different frequency responses depending on package size, process, and component type. Therefore, there is no universal frequency limit for capacitor decoupling performance. The effective frequency range depends on package size, equivalent series inductance (ESL), component characteristics, and the actual PCB layout. If capacitor selection or placement is inappropriate, multiple capacitors can introduce additional inductive loops. Capacitors with different parameters may also resonate at specific frequencies, potentially increasing rather than reducing PDS impedance. Capacitor frequency-response characteristics should therefore be considered before placement and selection. （ADC decoupling capacitor layout） 3. High-Frequency PDS and PCB Stackup Design The effective decoupling range of discrete capacitors depends on their electrical characteristics and PCB layout, and there is no universal high-frequency cutoff. As frequency increases, package parasitics and ESL increasingly limit the high-frequency performance of discrete capacitors. At higher frequencies, the intrinsic capacitance formed between PCB power and ground planes becomes an important part of PDS design. Proper stackup design can therefore complement conventional discrete decoupling. Six-Layer PCB Stackup A typical six-layer PCB stackup can be arranged as: Top Signal → Ground 1 → Power 1 → Power 2 → Ground 2 → Bottom Signal In high-speed PCB design, keeping the dielectric thickness between adjacent power and ground planes relatively small, such as a typical range of 2–4 mil, helps increase plane capacitance and reduce the impedance of high-frequency current paths. This optimization is achieved primarily through the PCB stackup and does not require additional components. The required stackup and dielectric thickness simply need to be specified in the PCB fabrication documentation. Eight-Layer PCB Stackup Optimization For an eight-layer PCB, additional ground reference layers can be introduced while maintaining a small core-layer spacing, such as 2–3 mil. This can significantly increase the intrinsic plane capacitance, although the actual increase is not necessarily double. It depends on dielectric thickness, copper area, and the overall configuration of the power and ground layers. Compared with simply adding more high-frequency discrete capacitors, stackup optimization can reduce component count and provide a cleaner high-frequency PDS structure. PDS Impedance and Dynamic Current The primary function of the PDS is to suppress voltage fluctuations caused by the dynamic current demand of the circuit. Low-impedance power and ground planes, combined with an appropriate PCB stackup, can reduce voltage fluctuations caused by rapidly changing currents. According to V = IR, if the dynamic current is 1 A and the PDS impedance is 10 mΩ, the corresponding voltage variation is approximately 10 mV. Optimizing the PCB stackup can extend the effective high-frequency low-impedance range, but overall PDS performance is also affected by power-plane integrity, ground-via placement, package parasitics, and local current-loop design. Therefore, conventional low-frequency decoupling capacitors can be placed at key locations such as power-entry points, high-power devices, and surge-current devices. Combining different decoupling mechanisms can help optimize PDS impedance over a broad frequency range. Dense capacitor placement around every IC is not always necessary and may introduce unnecessary cost, space consumption, and resonance risks. （discrete vs plane capacitance） 4. PCB Layer-to-Layer Coupling and Noise Suppression In multilayer PCB layouts, sensitive analog layers, including analog power, ground, and signal layers, can experience crosstalk when placed close to high-frequency digital layers. Because some noise sources are located directly above or below sensitive analog layers, this type of coupling can easily be overlooked. Layer Coupling in ADC Layout Adjacent PCB conductor layers form parasitic capacitive structures, which can produce electric-field coupling under certain frequency and layout conditions. The actual coupling level has no fixed value and depends on factors such as layer spacing, dielectric thickness, copper area, routing length, signal edge rate, return path, and interlayer parasitic capacitance. For example, if simulation or measurement confirms that a high-speed digital signal produces approximately 1 mV of interference at a sensitive analog node through layer coupling, this interference corresponds to about 2 LSB for a 12-bit ADC with a 2 Vpp full-scale range and about 8 LSB for a 14-bit ADC. In high-resolution ADC systems, such coupling can significantly reduce signal margin and system SNR. Therefore, during ADC layout, the signal characteristics of adjacent layers should be carefully evaluated. High-noise digital layers should be kept away from sensitive analog layers where practical, while appropriate stackup, routing, and return-path design should be used to reduce interlayer coupling. 5. Analog and Digital Grounding in ADC PCB Design In ADC PCB design, there is no universal requirement to divide the ground plane into analog ground (AGND) and digital ground (DGND). The appropriate approach depends on the device manufacturer's recommendations, system partitioning, and current return paths. In many conventional applications, a continuous ground plane is preferable to unnecessary segmentation. （Backflow Path） Why Avoid Unnecessary Ground Plane Splitting? Unnecessary ground-plane splitting can increase the inductance of current return paths. According to V = L(di/dt), higher return-path inductance increases transient voltage noise caused by rapidly changing currents and may also worsen the high-frequency impedance characteristics of the local power and ground network. As ADC sampling rates increase, switching currents can change more rapidly, making parasitic inductance in the return path increasingly important. Therefore, a continuous ground plane should generally be maintained unless system requirements indicate otherwise. Optimize ADC Return Paths Through Functional Partitioning The core of grounding design is functional partitioning and return-path optimization. By separating analog and digital circuits through appropriate component placement and controlling the return paths of high-speed digital signals, unwanted interaction between analog and digital sections can be reduced. In many applications, proper PCB layout, a continuous ground reference plane, and controlled return paths can provide good grounding performance without physically splitting the ground plane. Should AGND and DGND Be Connected at a Single Point? Ground-plane segmentation may be considered when layout constraints prevent effective functional partitioning or when high-noise digital circuits and power buses cannot be sufficiently separated from sensitive analog circuitry. However, a single-point AGND-DGND connection is not universally appropriate for every ADC system. The grounding method should be selected based on device characteristics, PCB return-path distribution, and overall system noise performance, with the device datasheet and system requirements serving as the primary references. 6. High-Speed ADC Layout Design Summary High-speed ADC layout should focus on the key factors that directly affect signal-chain performance rather than adding unnecessary design complexity. For system-level, module-level, and evaluation-board designs, a continuous ground plane can generally be preferred, with functional partitioning used to optimize return paths and reduce layer-to-layer coupling. PCB assembly processes can also directly affect system performance. Manufacturing documentation should specify EPAD segmentation, via treatment, and other relevant assembly requirements according to the device and manufacturing process to ensure reliable solder connections. Power decoupling should be based on accurate component selection and targeted placement. Combined with a PCB stackup that places power and ground planes closely together, this approach can improve high-frequency decoupling performance. Conventional low-frequency decoupling capacitors can then be used at appropriate locations to optimize PDS impedance over a broad frequency range. For high-speed analog-to-digital converter applications, ADC PCB design should be adapted to the specific system requirements. A well-planned ADC layout should focus on device connectivity, power integrity, high-frequency impedance, layer-to-layer coupling, and grounding and return paths. By addressing these factors together, designers can improve the stability and overall performance of high-speed ADC systems. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > How to Properly Handle Unused IC Pins in Schematic Design How to Properly Handle Unused IC Pins in Schematic Design by: Mila Sep 09,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout schematic design cmos pins nc pins When working on schematic design , engineers often encounter situations like this: to meet the core functional requirements, a 100-pin MCU is selected, but only 60 pins are actually used. Or a 4-channel op-amp is selected, but only three channels are needed. Some ICs may also have pins marked as NC. Seeing all those pins labeled as "Not Connected" on the schematic can be confusing. Should these unused pins simply be left floating? Should they be connected to ground? Or should they be connected to a power supply? Improper handling of unused pins can lead to undefined input states, increased power consumption, or noise interference, and in severe cases may even affect device reliability. This article explains how to properly handle these seemingly minor but important details in schematic design. 1. Why Should Unused IC Pins Be Handled Carefully? Many ICs today use CMOS technology. One key rule to remember is: do not leave CMOS inputs floating, especially digital input pins. （CMOS device） This can be understood from the internal structure of CMOS circuits. A typical CMOS input stage consists of an inverter made up of a PMOS and an NMOS connected in series. When the input is low, the PMOS is on and the NMOS is off. When the input is high, the PMOS is off and the NMOS is on. Under ideal static conditions, only a very small leakage current flows, giving CMOS circuits very low static power consumption. 2. What Happens When CMOS Pins Are Left Floating? What happens when an input is left floating? Because the input has very high impedance, it can easily be affected by surrounding electromagnetic noise, parasitic coupling, and leakage current. As a result, the input voltage may become undefined and fluctuate between low and high levels. When the input voltage falls within the transition region of the CMOS input stage, the PMOS and NMOS may both be partially turned on, causing increased supply current. In other words, floating CMOS pins have no guaranteed logic state, so it is impossible to reliably determine whether the input will be interpreted as a high or low level. 3. How to Handle Unused MCU GPIOs? Modern MCUs usually provide multifunctional GPIOs. For unused GPIOs, follow the requirements in the device datasheet and configure the corresponding IO as an output with a defined state, such as driving it low or high. If supported by the device, it can also be configured as an input with an internal pull-up or pull-down. When permitted by the device, this eliminates the need for external pull-up or pull-down resistors, saving components and PCB space. For critical pins such as interrupt, reset, and mode-selection pins, however, their default logic states should be clearly defined. Whether an external pull-up or pull-down resistor is required should be determined according to the datasheet and reference design to prevent unintended triggering. 4. How to Handle Unused Op-Amp Channels? Op-amps and ADCs require special attention because analog circuits are more sensitive to noise, and their unused pins may need to be handled differently from digital circuits. For example, if you use a dual-channel op-amp but only need one channel, what should you do with the unused channel? （IC Pins） Leaving it floating is generally not recommended because the input pins can pick up noise, causing the output to saturate and potentially increasing power consumption. What if both the non-inverting and inverting inputs are connected to ground? This puts the op-amp in an open-loop configuration, so its output may not be well controlled. For a typical voltage-feedback op-amp, if permitted by the datasheet, a better approach is to configure the unused channel as a voltage follower: connect the output to the inverting input to create negative feedback, and connect the non-inverting input to GND. However, the op-amp's input common-mode range and output swing must also be checked to ensure that this configuration is within the device's specifications. 5. What About Unused ADC Inputs? Unused ADC channels should be handled according to the device datasheet. Some devices recommend connecting unused ADC inputs to GND or another stable reference level to prevent the channel from picking up noise. However, directly connecting the input to ground should not be treated as a universal rule for all ADCs. Therefore, unused ADC inputs should not simply be treated in the same way as digital GPIOs. Always check the manufacturer's recommended connection method before finalizing the schematic design. 6. What Do NC Pins Mean on an IC? IC datasheets often contain pins marked as NC, or "No Connect." These NC pins need to be examined carefully. NC does not necessarily mean that the pin can be connected in any way. Some NC pins may have no internal connection and should simply be left floating. However, other pins marked as NC may have internal connections related to testing, reserved functions, or other circuits. The handling method must strictly follow the datasheet. For example, some datasheets specify "Must be left floating," while others specify "Must be tied to GND." If you connect NC pins to ground without checking the datasheet, you could potentially cause unexpected behavior or interfere with internal test or reserved functions. 7. The Key Rule: Always Check the Datasheet When dealing with unused IC pins, the most important principle is not simply whether a pin should be left floating or connected to ground. Instead, first identify the pin type and then follow the connection requirements specified in the datasheet. （DBV package） Different types of GPIOs, analog inputs, op-amp channels, and NC pins may require completely different handling methods. In simple terms: Unused GPIOs: Configure them to a defined state according to the datasheet. Critical input pins: Make sure they have a clearly defined default logic level. Unused op-amp channels: Use a stable negative-feedback configuration when recommended. Unused ADC inputs: Follow the device manufacturer's recommended connection method. NC pins: Strictly follow the datasheet requirements. A simple "Not Connected" label on a schematic may involve power consumption, noise, stability, and even device reliability. Do not rely on assumptions. Check the datasheet first, then decide how the pin should be connected. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > USB Type-C Design and CC Pin Configuration: A Practical Hardware Design Guide USB Type-C Design and CC Pin Configuration: A Practical Hardware Design Guide by: Mila Sep 08,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout hardware design type c design usb design usb type c design usb pcb design One of the most common pitfalls in Hardware Design for Type-C interfaces is confusing the legacy protocols used by USB-A ports with the native USB Type-C protocol. Some designers mistakenly treat D+ / D− as the core charging detection pins of Type-C, which can lead to design failures. The voltage is a normal 5V, the polarity is correct, but the device still does not charge, fails to be recognized, only works in one plug orientation, or has limited charging current. Compatibility issues may also occur with some phones. In many cases, there is basically one reason: CC1 and CC2 are not connected correctly. Let's look at the most common 5V Type-C charging configuration. Once you understand it, you can use it directly in your Type C Design. 1. The Most Important Conclusion For a Type-C interface, CC1 / CC2 are the core channels for power role detection, connection detection, current capability detection, and USB PD communication. D+ and D− do not handle basic Type-C power detection or USB PD negotiation in a standard C-to-C connection. This is one of the key differences between traditional USB and modern USB Type C Design: CC pins: The dedicated Type-C configuration channel used for power role detection, connection detection, plug orientation detection, Type-C current capability detection, and USB PD communication. D+ / D− pins: Mainly used for USB 2.0 data transmission and compatibility with certain legacy charging protocols, such as BC1.2. In simple terms: C-to-C charging: Basic power detection mainly relies on CC, not D+ / D−. A-to-C charging: Legacy USB-A charging protocols may use D+ / D− for charging detection. 2. Why Does C-to-C Charging Mainly Rely on CC? Taking a standard USB-C-to-USB-C charging connection as an example, the Source and Sink first establish a connection through the CC pins. The basic process is: 1. The charger provides Rp pull-ups on CC1 and CC2. 2. The phone or other powered device uses Rd pull-downs to indicate that it is a Sink. 3. The two sides detect the connection and determine the available Type-C current capability through CC. 4. If both sides support USB PD, they can further communicate through the CC channel to negotiate voltage, current, and power. It is important to note that 56KΩ, 22KΩ, and 10KΩ Rp values correspond to different advertised current capabilities. They should not be interpreted as “56KΩ directly unlocks 5V/3A.” Therefore, Type-C current capability detection and USB PD fast charging should be distinguished: Type-C current capability detection → Rp / Rd USB PD power negotiation → PD communication over CC D+ / D− mainly handle USB 2.0 data and certain legacy charging protocols. 3. CC vs. D+ / D−: What Does Each One Actually Do? CC1 / CC2: The Core Type-C Power and Connection Pins CC stands for Configuration Channel and is an important feature that distinguishes USB Type-C from traditional USB-A interfaces. CC1 and CC2 are mainly responsible for: Power role detection: Rp indicates a Source, while Rd indicates a Sink. Connection detection: Determines whether a valid connection has been established. Plug orientation detection: The active CC pin helps determine the plug orientation. Type-C current capability detection: The Source uses Rp to advertise its power capability. USB PD communication: USB PD devices use the CC channel to negotiate voltage, current, and power. Therefore, in a standard Type-C C-to-C power connection: Correct CC configuration is critical to proper device detection and power delivery. This is why CC routing and component placement are important in USB PCB Design. D+ / D−: Data Transmission and Legacy Charging Compatibility D+ / D− are essentially USB 2.0 differential data lines. They are mainly used for: 1. USB 2.0 data transmission, programming, and communication 2. Compatibility with certain legacy USB-A charging protocols For example, USB BC1.2 charging detection mechanisms may use D+ / D−. The key distinction is: C-to-C architecture: Basic Type-C power detection relies on CC. A-to-C architecture: Legacy USB-A charging protocols may involve D+ / D−. Therefore, the fact that D+ / D− were widely used for charging detection in the USB-A era does not mean that they are required for basic charging in a USB-C-to-USB-C connection. This distinction is important in practical USB Design . 4. Three Common CC Configurations + Applicable Scenarios The most common Type-C CC configurations can be divided into three categories: Sink, Source, and DRP. Typical resistor values include: Rp = 56KΩ / 22KΩ / 10KΩ Rd = 5.1KΩ The exact configuration depends on the device role and the Type-C / USB PD requirements. Configuration 1: Dual 5.1KΩ Pull-Down Resistors on CC1 / CC2 Typical connection: CC1 → 5.1KΩ → GND CC2 → 5.1KΩ → GND Applicable to: Phones, development boards, microcontroller boards, small appliances, and other Type-C devices that work as Sink devices. Function: The device indicates that it is a powered device, allowing the Source to detect the connection and determine the plug orientation. For basic Type-C power, this configuration can support standard 5V operation. Note: Two 5.1KΩ resistors do not automatically give the device USB PD fast-charging capability. If the device needs 9V, 12V, 15V, 20V, or other USB PD voltages, an appropriate USB PD Controller and supporting power-management circuitry are normally required. （Pull-Down Resistors） Configuration 2: Dual Rp Pull-Up Resistors on CC1 / CC2 Typical connection: CC1 → Rp → VBUS CC2 → Rp → VBUS Applicable to: Standard USB Type-C chargers, power banks with Type-C output ports, and other devices that work as a Source. Function: The Source uses CC to advertise its power capability so that the connected Type-C device can identify the power source. Different Rp configurations correspond to different Type-C default current capabilities. If USB PD fast charging is required, the design needs to support PD communication through the CC channel rather than relying on Rp alone. If compatibility with legacy USB-A charging protocols is also required, additional D+ / D− charging-detection circuitry or a charging protocol IC can be added according to the product requirements. （Pull-Up Resistors） Configuration 3: Dynamic Rp / Rd Switching for DRP Applicable to: Expansion docks, power banks, portable energy-storage devices, and other Type-C devices that need to dynamically switch between Source and Sink roles. Function: The device can determine its role according to the connected device and connection state, allowing it to operate as either a power source or a powered device. Note: DRP does not simply mean connecting Rp and Rd to CC1 / CC2 at the same time. In practical designs, a Type-C Controller or USB PD Controller is typically used to dynamically manage Rp / Rd, together with power-path control for safe bidirectional power delivery. （Rp / Rd Switching Resistors） Configuration 4: Type-C + USB PD Controller for Fast Charging If the product needs more than basic 5V power, such as: 9V / 12V / 15V / 20V or needs: Voltage, current, and power negotiation then Rp / Rd resistors alone are not sufficient. A typical architecture is: CC1 / CC2 → USB PD Controller → Power Path / DC-DC The PD Controller communicates through the CC channel and controls the downstream power circuitry according to the negotiated power profile. For USB Type C Design , this distinction is important when moving from basic 5V charging to USB PD fast charging. 5. A Common Mistake: Do Not Simply Short CC1 and CC2 Together Some Type-C designs try to make the interface work in both orientations by simply connecting: CC1 + CC2 → Shorted → One Rp or Rd. This should not be treated as a standard Type-C CC configuration. Simply shorting CC1 and CC2 can cause problems with proper connection detection and orientation handling, and may lead to compatibility issues in some applications. This is especially important for designs involving USB PD, higher current levels, or E-Marker cables. The correct approach is to configure the CC pins according to the required device role: Sink: CC1 → Rd CC2 → Rd Source: CC1 → Rp CC2 → Rp DRP: CC1 / CC2 → Type-C / PD Controller for dynamic role management Therefore, in USB PCB Design, CC1 and CC2 should be treated as separate configuration paths rather than simply tying them together. （CC1 and CC2 are shorted） 6. Final Takeaway: Check CC Before D+ / D− If you are designing a basic Type-C 5V Sink interface, the first thing to remember is simple: CC1 and CC2 each use a 5.1KΩ pull-down resistor to GND. For a Type-C Source, select the appropriate Rp configuration according to the required power capability. If the product requires: Bidirectional charging → DRP 9V / 12V / 15V / 20V → USB PD Higher-current applications → Consider USB PD, cable capability, E-Marker requirements, and the complete power path D+ / D− should be determined separately according to whether the product needs: USB 2.0 data transmissionOr Legacy USB-A charging protocol compatibility. The biggest pitfall in Type-C Hardware Design is not simply whether VBUS measures 5V. The key is whether the interface correctly follows the USB Type-C rules for CC1 / CC2, Rp, Rd, DRP, and USB PD. Verify Now Blog > USB Type-C Design and CC Pin Configuration: A Practical Hardware Design Guide USB Type-C Design and CC Pin Configuration: A Practical Hardware Design Guide by: Mila Sep 08,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout hardware design type c design usb design usb type c design usb pcb design One of the most common pitfalls in Hardware Design for Type-C interfaces is confusing the legacy protocols used by USB-A ports with the native USB Type-C protocol. Some designers mistakenly treat D+ / D− as the core charging detection pins of Type-C, which can lead to design failures. The voltage is a normal 5V, the polarity is correct, but the device still does not charge, fails to be recognized, only works in one plug orientation, or has limited charging current. Compatibility issues may also occur with some phones. In many cases, there is basically one reason: CC1 and CC2 are not connected correctly. Let's look at the most common 5V Type-C charging configuration. Once you understand it, you can use it directly in your Type C Design. 1. The Most Important Conclusion For a Type-C interface, CC1 / CC2 are the core channels for power role detection, connection detection, current capability detection, and USB PD communication. D+ and D− do not handle basic Type-C power detection or USB PD negotiation in a standard C-to-C connection. This is one of the key differences between traditional USB and modern USB Type C Design: CC pins: The dedicated Type-C configuration channel used for power role detection, connection detection, plug orientation detection, Type-C current capability detection, and USB PD communication. D+ / D− pins: Mainly used for USB 2.0 data transmission and compatibility with certain legacy charging protocols, such as BC1.2. In simple terms: C-to-C charging: Basic power detection mainly relies on CC, not D+ / D−. A-to-C charging: Legacy USB-A charging protocols may use D+ / D− for charging detection. 2. Why Does C-to-C Charging Mainly Rely on CC? Taking a standard USB-C-to-USB-C charging connection as an example, the Source and Sink first establish a connection through the CC pins. The basic process is: 1. The charger provides Rp pull-ups on CC1 and CC2. 2. The phone or other powered device uses Rd pull-downs to indicate that it is a Sink. 3. The two sides detect the connection and determine the available Type-C current capability through CC. 4. If both sides support USB PD, they can further communicate through the CC channel to negotiate voltage, current, and power. It is important to note that 56KΩ, 22KΩ, and 10KΩ Rp values correspond to different advertised current capabilities. They should not be interpreted as “56KΩ directly unlocks 5V/3A.” Therefore, Type-C current capability detection and USB PD fast charging should be distinguished: Type-C current capability detection → Rp / Rd USB PD power negotiation → PD communication over CC D+ / D− mainly handle USB 2.0 data and certain legacy charging protocols. 3. CC vs. D+ / D−: What Does Each One Actually Do? CC1 / CC2: The Core Type-C Power and Connection Pins CC stands for Configuration Channel and is an important feature that distinguishes USB Type-C from traditional USB-A interfaces. CC1 and CC2 are mainly responsible for: Power role detection: Rp indicates a Source, while Rd indicates a Sink. Connection detection: Determines whether a valid connection has been established. Plug orientation detection: The active CC pin helps determine the plug orientation. Type-C current capability detection: The Source uses Rp to advertise its power capability. USB PD communication: USB PD devices use the CC channel to negotiate voltage, current, and power. Therefore, in a standard Type-C C-to-C power connection: Correct CC configuration is critical to proper device detection and power delivery. This is why CC routing and component placement are important in USB PCB Design. D+ / D−: Data Transmission and Legacy Charging Compatibility D+ / D− are essentially USB 2.0 differential data lines. They are mainly used for: 1. USB 2.0 data transmission, programming, and communication 2. Compatibility with certain legacy USB-A charging protocols For example, USB BC1.2 charging detection mechanisms may use D+ / D−. The key distinction is: C-to-C architecture: Basic Type-C power detection relies on CC. A-to-C architecture: Legacy USB-A charging protocols may involve D+ / D−. Therefore, the fact that D+ / D− were widely used for charging detection in the USB-A era does not mean that they are required for basic charging in a USB-C-to-USB-C connection. This distinction is important in practical USB Design . 4. Three Common CC Configurations + Applicable Scenarios The most common Type-C CC configurations can be divided into three categories: Sink, Source, and DRP. Typical resistor values include: Rp = 56KΩ / 22KΩ / 10KΩ Rd = 5.1KΩ The exact configuration depends on the device role and the Type-C / USB PD requirements. Configuration 1: Dual 5.1KΩ Pull-Down Resistors on CC1 / CC2 Typical connection: CC1 → 5.1KΩ → GND CC2 → 5.1KΩ → GND Applicable to: Phones, development boards, microcontroller boards, small appliances, and other Type-C devices that work as Sink devices. Function: The device indicates that it is a powered device, allowing the Source to detect the connection and determine the plug orientation. For basic Type-C power, this configuration can support standard 5V operation. Note: Two 5.1KΩ resistors do not automatically give the device USB PD fast-charging capability. If the device needs 9V, 12V, 15V, 20V, or other USB PD voltages, an appropriate USB PD Controller and supporting power-management circuitry are normally required. （Pull-Down Resistors） Configuration 2: Dual Rp Pull-Up Resistors on CC1 / CC2 Typical connection: CC1 → Rp → VBUS CC2 → Rp → VBUS Applicable to: Standard USB Type-C chargers, power banks with Type-C output ports, and other devices that work as a Source. Function: The Source uses CC to advertise its power capability so that the connected Type-C device can identify the power source. Different Rp configurations correspond to different Type-C default current capabilities. If USB PD fast charging is required, the design needs to support PD communication through the CC channel rather than relying on Rp alone. If compatibility with legacy USB-A charging protocols is also required, additional D+ / D− charging-detection circuitry or a charging protocol IC can be added according to the product requirements. （Pull-Up Resistors） Configuration 3: Dynamic Rp / Rd Switching for DRP Applicable to: Expansion docks, power banks, portable energy-storage devices, and other Type-C devices that need to dynamically switch between Source and Sink roles. Function: The device can determine its role according to the connected device and connection state, allowing it to operate as either a power source or a powered device. Note: DRP does not simply mean connecting Rp and Rd to CC1 / CC2 at the same time. In practical designs, a Type-C Controller or USB PD Controller is typically used to dynamically manage Rp / Rd, together with power-path control for safe bidirectional power delivery. （Rp / Rd Switching Resistors） Configuration 4: Type-C + USB PD Controller for Fast Charging If the product needs more than basic 5V power, such as: 9V / 12V / 15V / 20V or needs: Voltage, current, and power negotiation then Rp / Rd resistors alone are not sufficient. A typical architecture is: CC1 / CC2 → USB PD Controller → Power Path / DC-DC The PD Controller communicates through the CC channel and controls the downstream power circuitry according to the negotiated power profile. For USB Type C Design , this distinction is important when moving from basic 5V charging to USB PD fast charging. 5. A Common Mistake: Do Not Simply Short CC1 and CC2 Together Some Type-C designs try to make the interface work in both orientations by simply connecting: CC1 + CC2 → Shorted → One Rp or Rd. This should not be treated as a standard Type-C CC configuration. Simply shorting CC1 and CC2 can cause problems with proper connection detection and orientation handling, and may lead to compatibility issues in some applications. This is especially important for designs involving USB PD, higher current levels, or E-Marker cables. The correct approach is to configure the CC pins according to the required device role: Sink: CC1 → Rd CC2 → Rd Source: CC1 → Rp CC2 → Rp DRP: CC1 / CC2 → Type-C / PD Controller for dynamic role management Therefore, in USB PCB Design, CC1 and CC2 should be treated as separate configuration paths rather than simply tying them together. （CC1 and CC2 are shorted） 6. Final Takeaway: Check CC Before D+ / D− If you are designing a basic Type-C 5V Sink interface, the first thing to remember is simple: CC1 and CC2 each use a 5.1KΩ pull-down resistor to GND. For a Type-C Source, select the appropriate Rp configuration according to the required power capability. If the product requires: Bidirectional charging → DRP 9V / 12V / 15V / 20V → USB PD Higher-current applications → Consider USB PD, cable capability, E-Marker requirements, and the complete power path D+ / D− should be determined separately according to whether the product needs: USB 2.0 data transmissionOr Legacy USB-A charging protocol compatibility. The biggest pitfall in Type-C Hardware Design is not simply whether VBUS measures 5V. The key is whether the interface correctly follows the USB Type-C rules for CC1 / CC2, Rp, Rd, DRP, and USB PD. Once these concepts are clear, basic Type-C charging interfaces become much easier to design correctly. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac.
